item.title: ‘Activists of rhythm’: Fighting Spain’s far-right through art
item.description:
Santiago Abascal’s party has adopted radical ideas from France and beyond. If it joins a PP coalition, it would be a morale boost for allies across the continent It was a scene few would have imagined possible in Spanish politics until recently. Flanked on stage by Catalan flags, the far-right Vox leader, Santiago Abascal, addressed a packed campaign rally in Girona, where he promised “to defend Catalan identity” against supposed “Islamisation”. He urged his audience to confront what he claimed was “the primary challenge” of a new “caliphate” across Spain. For a fringe party that made its breakthrough in 2018 by demonising Catalonia’s independence movement, it was a striking change of emphasis, reflecting a strategic shift that has brought Vox to the brink of power. item.title: Canada's Supreme Court largely upholds a Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
item.description:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights. In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning , the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights. item.title: Polls open in Taiwan's closely watched local elections
item.description:
Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage. Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years , are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution. item.title: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights
item.description:
A Norse Atlantic Airways Boeing 787. PATRICK T. FALLON/AFP via Getty Images Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit filed for bankruptcy as it fights to stay in business. It also grounded its flights and received notices terminating the lease agreements for its fleet. Norse had been losing millions since fuel prices surged due to the Iran war. Cheap transatlantic flights are on the brink as Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy. The budget airline, which has previously offered one-way New York-to-London tickets for as little as $99, warned on Wednesday that its "financial situation is critical." On Friday, it announced that its Norwegian operating unit had filed for bankruptcy. All Norse flights are canceled, and ticket sales have been discontinued, it added. item.title: Open Thread
item.description:
People share food at the dinner table during Thanksgiving. —Stock photo—Getty Images As households across America prepare to gather for their Thanksgiving celebrations , there’s one question at the forefront of hosts’ minds: what time should dinner be served? A quick glance on social media will tell you that it’s a hotly-debated topic, and one that people have firm opinions on. Lifestyle expert Martha Stewart’s online publication conducted a poll in 2024, asking readers what time Thanksgiving dinner should start. More than 34,000 people joined the conversation, with the majority of respondents (13,586) saying the meal should begin between 2 to 3 p.m., local time. item.title: Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response
item.description:
⁠Ukraine made a Black Sea ceasefire offer to enable food exports and passed the details on to international allies, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday, adding that Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow. The announcement came a day after Russia attacked two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.
